docs.title: pyhood
docs.text:
Robinhood for AI agents: stocks, options, crypto and futures from the command line.

pyhood is a Robinhood client and command line built to be driven by an AI agent. You ask in plain language, the agent runs pyhood, and before anything is sent you see exactly what it will be. It is also a typed Python library for scripts that need to stay logged in.

New here? Getting Started has one command that installs pyhood and logs you in.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• 🤖 Made for AI agents — Commands an agent can run for positions, orders, quotes and option chains, a guide it reads first, and an AGENTS.md that ships in the install folder.
  • ✅ You choose how much it asks you — out of the box pyhood buy sends nothing until it is run again with the code it printed, so what is placed is what you were shown. Turn confirmation off and orders up to an amount you set are placed at once.
  • 🔐 Auth that just works — Login with timeouts, automatic token refresh, and session persistence.
  • 🔄 Automatic token refresh — OAuth refresh tokens renew your session silently — no credentials, no device approval, no human in the loop.
  • 🏷️ Type hints everywhere — Full type annotations, dataclass responses, IDE-friendly.
  • 🛡️ Built-in rate limiting — Automatic request throttling and retry logic.
  • 📊 Options-first — Deep options chain support with Greeks, volume/OI analysis, and earnings integration.
  • 📈 Futures trading — Contract details, real-time quotes, order history, and P&L calculation for futures.
  • 🪙 Dual API support — Wraps both Robinhood's unofficial stocks/options API and their official Crypto Trading API.
  • 🧪 Tested and maintained — CI across Python 3.10-3.14, linted with ruff, and audited against the live API.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
import pyhood
from pyhood.client import PyhoodClient

session = pyhood.login(username="you@email.com", password="...", timeout=90)
client = PyhoodClient(session)

quote = client.get_quote("AAPL")
print(f"AAPL: ${quote.price:.2f} ({quote.change_pct:+.1f}%)")

docs.title: All Accounts (Including IRA)
docs.text:
Robinhood's standard /accounts/ endpoint only returns your individual brokerage account. IRA accounts (Traditional, Roth) are hidden behind a different endpoint. pyhood handles this automatically.

accounts = client.get_all_accounts()

for acct in accounts:
    print(f"{acct.account_number} | {acct.account_type} | Cash: ${acct.cash:.2f}")

This uses Robinhood's bonfire endpoint internally to discover all linked accounts, including retirement accounts that don't appear in the standard API.

power = client.get_buying_power()

docs.title: IRA Buying Power
docs.text:
Pass account_number to check buying power for a specific account:

bp = client.get_buying_power(account_number="YOUR_IRA_ACCOUNT")
print(f"IRA buying power: ${bp:,.2f}")

docs.title: Positions
docs.text:
Get all current stock positions:

positions = client.get_positions()

for pos in positions:
    print(
        f"{pos.symbol:>6} | "
        f"Qty: {pos.quantity:.0f} | "
        f"Avg: ${pos.average_cost:.2f} | "
        f"Now: ${pos.current_price:.2f} | "
        f"P/L: ${pos.unrealized_pl:+.2f} ({pos.unrealized_pl_pct:+.1f}%)"
    )

docs.title: IRA / Retirement Accounts
docs.text: pyhood supports trading in Robinhood IRA accounts (Traditional and Roth). Most order methods accept an account_number parameter to target a specific account.

docs.title: Account Discovery
docs.text:
accounts = client.get_all_accounts()
ira = [a for a in accounts if "ira" in a.account_type.lower()]

docs.title: Trading in an IRA
docs.text:
Pass account_number to any order method:

# Buy stock in IRA
order = client.buy_stock(
    symbol="AAPL", quantity=10, price=180.00,
    account_number="YOUR_IRA_ACCOUNT",
)

# Buy options in IRA
order = client.buy_option(
    symbol="NKE", strike=55.0, expiration="2026-04-02",
    option_type="call", quantity=3, price=1.60,
    account_number="YOUR_IRA_ACCOUNT",
)

docs.title: IRA Limitations
docs.text:
• Cash account only — no margin, no day trading
  • Options: Level 2 max — long calls, long puts, covered calls, cash-secured puts
  • No spreads — multi-leg strategies are not available in IRA accounts
  • If account_number is omitted, orders default to your individual brokerage account

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
pyhood handles Robinhood's OAuth2 authentication with three layers of session management:

  1. Cached session — Reuse a valid stored token (instant)
  2. Token refresh — Exchange a refresh token for new credentials (no human needed)
  3. Full login — Username + password + device approval (requires phone)

When you call pyhood.login(), it tries each layer in order, falling back only when necessary.

The quickest way to establish a session is the setup command, which drives the same three layers and prompts only for what it actually needs:

pyhood authorize

See Setup for what it prompts for and how the tokens are stored.

docs.title: Login Flow
docs.text:
import pyhood

session = pyhood.login(
    username="you@email.com",
    password="your_password",
    timeout=90,
)

What happens internally:

  1. Check ~/.pyhood/session.json for a cached token
  2. If found, validate it against Robinhood's API
  3. If expired, try refreshing with the stored refresh token
  4. If refresh fails, perform a full login with device approval

docs.title: Token Refresh
docs.text:
This is pyhood's killer feature. The refresh token lets you renew your session without any human interaction:

import pyhood

# No username or password needed
session = pyhood.refresh()

Internally, this:

  • Sends the stored refresh_token to Robinhood's OAuth endpoint
  • Receives a new access_token and new refresh_token
  • Saves both to ~/.pyhood/session.json
  • Invalidates the old tokens (they rotate on each refresh)

Use pyhood.refresh() in cron jobs and automation

Since refresh requires no credentials and no device approval, it's the ideal entry point for unattended scripts. Only fall back to pyhood.login() if refresh raises TokenExpiredError.

docs.title: Token Lifetime
docs.text:
Token Observed Lifetime Notes Access token 5-8 days Robinhood sets this server-side; the expires_in parameter in the login request is ignored Refresh token Unknown (weeks+) Expires eventually; triggers TokenExpiredError

Note

Robinhood's token lifetimes are not documented and may change. pyhood handles expiration gracefully regardless of the actual lifetime.

docs.title: Device Approval
docs.text:
On first login (or when the refresh token expires), Robinhood requires device approval:

  1. pyhood sends your credentials to Robinhood
  2. Robinhood pushes a notification to your phone
  3. You tap "Yes, it's me" in the Robinhood app
  4. pyhood detects the approval and completes login

Device approval is phone app only — it's not available through the web interface.

docs.title: Timeouts
docs.text:
The timeout parameter controls how long pyhood waits for approval:

# Wait up to 2 minutes
session = pyhood.login(username="...", password="...", timeout=120)

If you don't approve in time, pyhood raises LoginTimeoutError.

docs.title: Session Storage
docs.text:
Tokens are stored in ~/.pyhood/session.json:

{
  "access_token": "eyJ...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "refresh_token": "abc...",
  "device_token": "12345-6789-...",
  "saved_at": 1710600000.0
}
  • device_token is preserved across sessions to minimize re-verification
  • saved_at tracks when tokens were last written
  • File permissions are your OS defaults — secure your machine accordingly

docs.title: Logout
docs.text:
To revoke tokens and delete stored credentials:

pyhood.logout()

This clears the session, removes ~/.pyhood/session.json, and attempts to revoke the token server-side.

docs.title: MFA / Two-Factor Authentication
docs.text:
If your Robinhood account uses SMS or email-based MFA:

from pyhood.exceptions import MFARequiredError

try:
    session = pyhood.login(username="...", password="...")
except MFARequiredError:
    code = input("Enter MFA code: ")
    session = pyhood.login(username="...", password="...", mfa_code=code)

docs.title: Command Line
docs.text:
The pyhood command answers the most common questions about an account without any code, and sets up and checks your login.

The account commands are read-only. The order commands change your account. Placing an order takes two steps, unless you have turned confirmation off: a first step that shows the order and sends nothing, then a second that places it. Cancelling one takes a single step.

docs.title: pyhood accounts
docs.text:
The accounts under your login, such as an individual account and an IRA, with what each is worth.

ACCOUNT     NUMBER      VALUE       CASH  BUYING POWER
Individual  …2223   $7,785.45    $168.85       $168.85
Roth IRA    …5556   $7,000.00  $7,000.00     $7,000.00

Account numbers show only their last four characters. --json gives them in full.

docs.title: --account
docs.text:
positions, orders and buying-power cover every account under your login. Add --account to see one. An order uses the first account unless it names another the same way. Name an account by part of its type, such as roth, ira or individual, or by the last four characters of its number.

pyhood positions --account roth
pyhood buy AAPL 10 --limit 350 --account roth

It works on positions, orders, buying-power, buy, sell, buy-option and sell-option. If what you type fits no account, or more than one, the command stops and lists your accounts. It does not guess.

docs.title: pyhood positions
docs.text:
What you hold: stocks, then options, with cost, value and unrealized profit or loss.

STOCKS
SYMBOL  SHARES  AVG COST    PRICE      VALUE  UNREALIZED P/L   P/L %
AAPL        10   $340.00  $352.01  $3,520.10        +$120.10  +3.53%
TOTAL                              $3,520.10        +$120.10

With more than one account, such as an individual account and an IRA, each is listed under its own heading:

Individual (…2223)

STOCKS
SYMBOL  SHARES  AVG COST    PRICE      VALUE  UNREALIZED P/L   P/L %
AAPL        10   $340.00  $352.01  $3,520.10        +$120.10  +3.53%
TOTAL                              $3,520.10        +$120.10

Roth IRA (…5556)

No open positions.

A stock held in two accounts shows as two positions, because each is sold from its own account. --account roth shows one account. With --json, stocks and options are the first account's and accounts lists them all.

Option prices are per share; one contract is 100 shares.

docs.text:
Stock and option orders in every account, newest first. With more than one account, an ACCOUNT column says which each order is in.

Orders since 2026-10-25 (times are EST; today is 2026-11-24)
PLACED                SIDE  SYMBOL  TYPE   ORDERED    LIMIT     STOP  FILLED  AVG PRICE  STATUS
2026-11-19 12:36 EST  buy   AAPL    stock       10  $350.00        -      10    $349.80  filled
2026-11-19 11:31 EST  buy   AAPL    stock       10  $340.00        -       0          -  cancelled
2026-11-18 10:02 EST  sell  AAPL    stock       10        -  $330.00       0          -  cancelled
Option Effect (none) Orders from the last 30 days --since YYYY-MM-DD Orders placed on or after that date --all Every order on record --symbol AAPL Orders for one symbol only --open Only orders that can still fill, which are the ones that can be cancelled --account roth One account's orders only

The last column is the order ID, which pyhood cancel takes.

An option order reads as a trade in a contract: buy to open under SIDE, and the contract, such as $12.00 call 2026-12-11, under TYPE. A spread shows as 2-leg option.

ORDERED is what was asked for and FILLED is what actually traded. They differ on a partial fill, such as an IPO Access allocation. An order that never filled shows 0 and -.

docs.title: pyhood buying-power
docs.text:
The cash available to trade with. With one account it is one line. With more than one, such as an individual account and an IRA, each account has its own row:

ACCOUNT     NUMBER  BUYING POWER
Individual  …2223        $168.85
Roth IRA    …5556      $7,000.00

The figures are not added up, because an account spends only its own cash: money in an IRA cannot pay for an order in another account. --account roth shows one account. With --json, buying_power is the first account's and accounts lists them all.

docs.title: pyhood quote SYMBOL [SYMBOL ...]
docs.text: Price, change, previous close, bid and ask for each symbol. Add --fundamentals for volume, P/E, market cap and the 52-week range, at the cost of one more request.

docs.title: pyhood dividends
docs.text: Dividends paid and pending, newest first, with the total paid. --symbol KO shows one stock's.

docs.title: pyhood transfers
docs.text:
Money moved in, out and between your accounts, newest first. It cannot make a transfer.

CREATED     AMOUNT     WHAT              FROM                       TO                  STATE      TRANSFER ID
2026-11-24  $100.00    deposit           Savings …1234 (Rainy day)  Individual account  pending    1a2b3c4d-...
2026-03-23  $7,000.00  IRA Contribution  Individual account         Roth IRA            completed  5e6f7a8b-...

A transfer with a bank is a deposit or a withdrawal, and the bank is named by its type, last four digits and nickname. The ID is what pyhood cancel-transfer takes, which works while a bank transfer is still pending. --json gives Robinhood's own record of each transfer.

docs.title: pyhood history SYMBOL
docs.text: Past prices: open, high, low, close and volume, with the change over the period. --span takes week, month (the default), 3month, year or 5year. The first three give one row a day, the last two one a week.

docs.title: pyhood earnings SYMBOL [SYMBOL ...]
docs.text: When each company next reports, whether before the open or after the close, and the estimate. --days N sets how far ahead to look; the default is 90.

docs.title: pyhood ratings SYMBOL [SYMBOL ...]
docs.text: Analysts' buy, hold and sell counts, and their low, mean and high price targets.

docs.title: pyhood news SYMBOL
docs.text: Recent headlines with their source, time and link. --count N sets how many; the default is 5.

docs.title: pyhood movers
docs.text: The S&P 500 stocks that have risen most today, with price and change. --down shows the biggest falls.

docs.title: Watchlists
docs.text:
pyhood watchlists              # your lists and what is on them
pyhood watch F GM              # add to 'My First List'
pyhood watch NVDA --list Tech  # add to another list
pyhood unwatch F               # take off

watch and unwatch act at once. No money is involved, so there is nothing to confirm. Each reads the list back afterwards and tells you if a symbol did not take.

docs.title: pyhood documents
docs.text:
Statements, trade confirmations and tax forms, newest first.

DATE        TYPE               DOCUMENT ID
2026-10-31  account_statement  1a2b3c4d-...
2026-02-10  1099               5e6f7a8b-...

--type narrows by any part of a type's name, such as statement, confirm, 1099 or 5498. --year 2026 narrows by year.

docs.title: pyhood document DOCUMENT_ID
docs.text:
Saves one document as a PDF, named for its date and type, such as 2026-10-31_account_statement.pdf. It goes into a documents folder where you are, or wherever --to FOLDER says.

A statement shows your account details, so the folder and the file are readable only by you. Nothing in your account changes.

docs.title: pyhood options SYMBOL
docs.text:
With only a symbol, the expiration dates of its options. With --expires, the contracts for that date nearest the stock's price:

$ pyhood options F --expires 2026-12-11 --strikes 4
F is at $11.95. Options expiring 2026-12-11 (17 days).
Prices are per share. One contract is 100 shares, so $2.50 costs $250.

CALLS, the 4 strikes nearest the price
STRIKE    BID    ASK   MARK   DELTA     IV  VOLUME  OPEN INT
$11.00  $0.89  $1.12  $1.01  +0.901  31.3%     117       209
$11.50  $0.60  $0.66  $0.63  +0.721  34.1%     253     1,558
$12.00  $0.28  $0.33  $0.31  +0.500  31.4%     560     3,547
$12.50  $0.11  $0.14  $0.13  +0.272  31.3%   1,171     1,467
Option Effect --expires YYYY-MM-DD Show the contracts for that expiration --call or --put Show one side only --strikes N How many strikes nearest the price to show. The default is 10

Delta and IV print as - when Robinhood publishes none, as on a contract's expiration day.

docs.title: --json
docs.text:
Each account command takes --json to print exact values in place of the table:

pyhood orders --symbol AAPL --json

Two differences from the tables:

  • Times are UTC, as Robinhood sends them, in ISO-8601 form. The tables convert them to your computer's time zone.
  • Unknown values are null, where the tables print -.

docs.title: Crypto
docs.text:
Crypto goes through Robinhood's official Crypto Trading API, which has its own credentials. Set them up once with pyhood setup crypto. A coin can be written BTC or BTC-USD.

pyhood crypto quote BTC ETH    # best bid and ask
pyhood crypto holdings         # the coins you hold, and crypto buying power
pyhood crypto orders           # crypto orders, newest first; --open for open ones

docs.title: Buying and selling
docs.text:
pyhood crypto buy and pyhood crypto sell work in the same two steps as stock orders. The quantity is in the coin, not in dollars.

$ pyhood crypto buy BTC 0.001 --limit 50000
NOT PLACED. This order needs your confirmation.

  Buy 0.001 BTC, limit $50,000.00
  Estimated cost:     $50.57 ($50.00 plus a fee of about $0.57)
  BTC now:            $60,000.00 to buy
  Buying power:       $500.00

  Note: The limit is 16.7% below the current price of $60,000.00.

  Note: A crypto limit order stays open until it fills or you cancel it.

To place this order, show this to the user. If they say yes, run:
  pyhood crypto buy BTC 0.001 --limit 50000 --confirm 4c1f0e

The first step differs from a stock order's in three ways:

  • It shows Robinhood's fee, as part of what a buy costs and taken off what a sale brings in. The fee comes from Robinhood's own estimate for that order.
  • It checks the coin can be traded through the API. Some coins trade in the app but not here, and those are refused.
  • It points out an order under Robinhood's minimum, which is a dollar value, about ten cents.

pyhood crypto cancel ORDER_ID cancels an open crypto order at once.

docs.title: Futures
docs.text:
Futures can be read, and an order estimated, but not placed. Name a product, such as ES for the E-mini S&P 500, NQ for the Nasdaq, CL for crude oil or GC for gold, and pyhood uses its nearest contract. You do not have to know which month is current.

pyhood futures quote ES NQ      # last, bid, ask, and the session's high, low and volume
pyhood futures contract ES      # the product's contracts and when each expires
pyhood futures contract ESZ26   # one contract: what a point and a tick are worth
pyhood futures orders           # orders, with realized profit and loss
pyhood futures positions        # open positions

$ pyhood futures quote ES
ES: the nearest contract is ESZ26, expiring 2026-12-18.
SYMBOL      LAST  CHANGE      BID       ASK   HIGH       LOW  PREV CLOSE  VOLUME
ESZ26   7,206.75  -0.15%  7,206.5  7,206.75  7,224  7,205.75     7,217.5   4,172

A contract can also be named in full, by product, month and year: ESZ26 is ES for December 2026.

pyhood futures positions prints what Robinhood sends without arranging it into columns. pyhood has not seen an open futures position, and does not guess at field names.

docs.title: Estimating a futures order
docs.text:
$ pyhood futures buy MES 1 --limit 5000
ESTIMATE ONLY. pyhood cannot place futures orders. Nothing has been sent.

  MES: the nearest contract is MESZ26, expiring 2026-12-18.
  Buy 1 MESZ26 contract, limit 5,000, good for day
  Contract:             Micro E-mini S&P 500 Stock Price Index Futures, Dec-26, expires 2026-12-18
  Position size:        $25,000.00 (1 x $5.00 a point x 5,000)
  MESZ26 now:           7,179.5 (bid 7,179.25, ask 7,179.5)
  Margin required:      $2,863.30
  Fees:                 $0.86, including $0.50 commission
  Buying power effect:  -$2,864.16
  Buying power after:   -$2,809.95
  Robinhood says:       it would refuse this order: not enough buying power.

This is an estimate only, and there is no step that places it. To place this order, use the Robinhood app or Robinhood Legend.
Option Effect --limit PRICE A limit order, with the price in the contract's points --market A market order --stop PRICE --market A stop order: it waits for the price, then trades at market --tif gtc Good till cancelled. The default is good for day --json The check as Robinhood reported it

The margin, the fees and the verdict are Robinhood's own. They come from the two requests its order ticket makes before it lets you submit an order, and neither places anything. Position size is worked out by pyhood: contracts, times dollars per point, times the price.

There is no --confirm, because there is nothing to confirm. pyhood has not seen the request that submits a futures order, so it does not send one. Robinhood offers limit, market and stop orders on futures, and no stop with a limit.

docs.title: Order commands
docs.text: Out of the box, pyhood buy and pyhood sell never act the first time they are run. You can change that: see Turning confirmation off.

docs.title: Step 1: see the order
docs.text:
$ pyhood buy AAPL 10 --limit 350
NOT PLACED. This order needs your confirmation.

  Buy 10 AAPL, limit $350.00, good for day
  Estimated cost:     $3,500.00
  AAPL now:           $352.01 (bid $351.99, ask $352.01)
  Buying power:       $5,000.00
  Market open:        yes

To place this order, show this to the user. If they say yes, run:
  pyhood buy AAPL 10 --limit 350 --confirm 98dee3

This step reads your quote, buying power or holdings, and points out anything that looks wrong:

  • the cost is more than your buying power
  • a sell is for more shares than you hold
  • the limit is 5% or more away from the last price
  • the order is a market order, which fills at whatever price is available

docs.title: Step 2: confirm
docs.text:
Run the command the first step printed. The order is placed and its status reported:

$ pyhood buy AAPL 10 --limit 350 --confirm 98dee3
PLACED: Buy 10 AAPL, limit $350.00, good for day
  Status:    confirmed
  Order ID:  1a2b3c4d-...

Check it with:  pyhood orders --symbol AAPL
Cancel it with: pyhood cancel 1a2b3c4d-...

docs.title: The confirmation code
docs.text:
The code is worked out from the order itself and today's date. So:

  • What is placed is what was shown. A different symbol, quantity, price or duration has a different code, and the wrong code is refused before anything is sent.
  • The order is always shown first, because that is the only place the code appears.
  • A code stops working at the end of the day.

It is a guardrail against mistakes, not a lock: anything that can run the first step can read the code. It makes an agent show its work. It does not stop an agent that ignores its instructions.

docs.title: Turning confirmation off
docs.text:
If you would rather your agent placed orders without asking, turn confirmation off. Run this yourself, in your own terminal:

$ pyhood setup confirmation off
Turning confirmation off means:
  - An order worth up to $5,000.00 is sent to Robinhood as soon as your
    agent runs it. You are not shown it first and are not asked.
  ...
Type yes to turn confirmation off: yes

Confirmation is off. Orders up to $5,000.00 are placed at once.

After that an order is placed on the first run:

$ pyhood buy AAPL 10 --limit 350
Confirmation is off and this order is not above $5,000.00, so it is sent at once.

  Buy 10 AAPL, limit $350.00, good for day
  Estimated cost:     $3,500.00
  AAPL now:           $352.01 (bid $351.99, ask $352.01)
  Buying power:       $5,000.00
  Market open:        yes

PLACED: Buy 10 AAPL, limit $350.00, good for day
  Status:    queued
  Order ID:  ...
Command What it does pyhood setup confirmation Shows the setting pyhood setup confirmation off Orders are placed at once, except above your amount pyhood setup confirmation above 500 Sets the amount. An order worth more still asks pyhood setup confirmation on Every order asks first. This is how pyhood starts

How it behaves:

  • The amount is a backstop. It starts at $5,000. An order worth more is not refused: it takes the usual two steps, and says why.
  • It measures what the order is worth: the estimated cost or proceeds the first step shows. Selling counts the same as buying. An option order counts its whole cost, 100 shares a contract.
  • Each order is judged on its own. Several orders under the amount all go through. It catches a mistake, such as 100 shares for 10. It is not a spending limit.
  • An order whose worth cannot be worked out asks.
  • --ask makes one order ask, whatever the setting.
  • Bank transfers always ask. Cancelling never does.
  • Warnings are still printed, above the line that says the order was placed. By then it has been sent.
  • The agent is told. pyhood guide describes whichever way this install is set, with the amount.

Turning confirmation off, or changing the amount, needs a person at the terminal. Run by an agent, the command changes nothing and tells the agent to ask you. Turning it back on works from anywhere. The setting is kept in ~/.pyhood/settings.json; an agent that can run commands could edit that file by hand, so this too is a guardrail and not a lock.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Command pyhood buy SYMBOL QUANTITY --limit PRICE Buy at that price or better pyhood buy SYMBOL QUANTITY --market Buy at the best price available pyhood sell SYMBOL QUANTITY --limit PRICE Sell at that price or better pyhood sell SYMBOL QUANTITY --market Sell at the best price available Option Effect --limit PRICE or --market One is required. There is no default --stop PRICE Make it a stop order. See below --trail-percent PERCENT or --trail-amount DOLLARS Make it a trailing stop. See below --account WHICH Place it in another account, such as roth --tif gfd Good for day. The default --tif gtc Good till cancelled --extended-hours Allow the order to trade outside regular hours --confirm CODE Place the order, using the code the first step printed --ask Ask first for this order, even with confirmation off

docs.title: Orders by dollar amount
docs.text:
--dollars AMOUNT in place of a number of shares buys or sells that much money's worth, which is usually a fraction of a share.

pyhood buy AAPL --dollars 50 --market

It is always a market order, in regular hours, of at least $1: Robinhood takes a fraction of a share no other way. The first step shows roughly how many shares the amount comes to.

A buy by dollar amount has been placed for real, with the market closed so that it could be cancelled before it traded. A sell by dollar amount has not.

docs.title: Stop orders
docs.text:
--stop PRICE makes an order wait. Nothing happens until the stock reaches the stop price; then the --market or --limit order is placed.

pyhood sell AAPL 10 --stop 340 --market --tif gtc   # sell if it falls to $340
pyhood sell AAPL 10 --stop 340 --limit 338 --tif gtc   # ... but not below $338

The first step points out two things that catch people:

  • A stop that would trigger at once. A sell stop belongs below the current price and a buy stop above it.
  • A stop that lasts only for today. Orders are good for the day by default, and a stop meant as protection is no use once it has expired. Add --tif gtc.

docs.title: Trailing stops
docs.text:
--trail-percent PERCENT or --trail-amount DOLLARS makes a stop that follows the price, staying that far behind its best level.

pyhood sell AAPL 10 --trail-percent 5 --market --tif gtc

The first step shows where the stop starts. It is always a market order for a number of shares.

A trailing stop that sells has been placed for real. One that buys has not yet, and the first step says so. If Robinhood refuses an order, nothing is placed and the reason is printed.

docs.title: Option orders
docs.text:
pyhood buy-option and pyhood sell-option work in the same two steps. Every term of the contract is named, and none has a default:

$ pyhood buy-option F --expires 2026-12-11 --strike 12 --call --contracts 1 --limit 0.30
NOT PLACED. This order needs your confirmation.

  Buy to open 1 contract of F $12.00 call expiring 2026-12-11, limit $0.30 per share, good for day
  Estimated cost:     $30.00 (1 contract x 100 shares x $0.30)
  Contract now:       mark $0.31 (bid $0.28, ask $0.33)
  F now:              $11.95
  Delta, IV:          +0.500, 31.4%
  Expires:            2026-12-11 (17 days)
  Buying power:       $500.00
  Market open:        yes

To place this order, show this to the user. If they say yes, run:
  pyhood buy-option F --expires 2026-12-11 --strike 12 --call --contracts 1 --limit 0.3 --confirm fdf2a6
Option Effect --expires YYYY-MM-DD The contract's expiration. Required --strike PRICE The contract's strike. Required --call or --put Required --contracts N How many contracts, each 100 shares. Required --limit PRICE Per share, as option prices are quoted: 2.50 is $250 a contract. Required; there are no market orders for options --to open or --to close Whether the order opens a position or closes one. A buy opens and a sell closes unless you say otherwise --tif gfd or --tif gtc Good for day (the default) or good till cancelled

The first step checks that the contract exists and names the nearest expirations or strikes if it does not. It also points out:

  • a cost of more than your buying power
  • a sell to close of more contracts than you hold
  • a sell to open, which writes a contract and takes on its obligation
  • a limit 20% or more from the contract's mark, which catches a price typed per contract in place of per share
  • a contract that expires today

docs.title: Spreads
docs.text:
pyhood spread places two to four option contracts as one order, for one net price.

$ pyhood spread F --expires 2026-12-11 --leg buy:call:12 --leg sell:call:13 --contracts 1 --debit 0.25
NOT PLACED. This order needs your confirmation.

  Open 1 F spread for a debit of $0.25 per share, good for day
    buy  $12.00 call 2026-12-11   mark $0.31 (bid $0.29, ask $0.33)
    sell $13.00 call 2026-12-11   mark $0.04 (bid $0.02, ask $0.06)
  Estimated cost:     $25.00 (1 spread x 100 shares x $0.25)
  Spread now:         about $0.27 debit at the marks, $0.31 debit to trade at once
  F now:              $11.95
Option Effect --expires YYYY-MM-DD The expiration of every leg that does not name its own. Required --leg SIDE:TYPE:STRIKE One contract: buy:call:350, sell:put:340. Give it two to four times. Add :YYYY-MM-DD for a leg with its own expiration --contracts N How many spreads. Required --debit PRICE or --credit PRICE The most to pay, or the least to accept, per share. One is required --to open or --to close Opening is the default --tif, --account As for other orders

The first step checks that every leg is a real contract, and prices the spread from its legs. It points out:

  • legs the wrong way round. If you ask for a debit but the legs as written pay a credit, the bought and sold legs are probably swapped.
  • a price 20% or more from what the spread is worth at the marks.

pyhood has not placed a spread against Robinhood. The order is built the way other clients build it and is covered by tests, but start with one contract.

docs.title: Cancelling an order
docs.text:
$ pyhood cancel 1a2b3c4d-...
CANCELLED: buy 10 AAPL, limit $350.00, placed 2026-11-24 16:54 EST

$ pyhood cancel 5e6f7a8b-...
CANCELLED: buy to open 1 F $12.00 call 2026-12-11, limit $0.30 per share, placed 2026-11-24 17:17 EST

pyhood cancel ORDER_ID acts at once, for stock and option orders alike. There is no first step and no code. A cancel names one order and can only remove it, so there is no symbol, quantity or price to get wrong, and when you want out of an order a second step is time in which it can fill.

  • Find the ID with pyhood orders --open.
  • An order that has already finished is left alone, and the command says so.
  • A cancel is a request. If the order filled before it landed, the command reports that in place of CANCELLED, and any part that had already filled is not undone.

These cover stock orders by shares or by dollar amount, stop orders and trailing stops, single-leg option orders and spreads, in any of your accounts, and crypto orders. Futures orders cannot be placed, from the command line or from Python. They can be estimated: see Estimating a futures order.

docs.title: Moving money
docs.text:
pyhood deposit and pyhood withdraw move money between a linked bank account and Robinhood. They always take two steps, whatever your confirmation setting.

$ pyhood withdraw 500
NOT SENT. This transfer needs your confirmation.

  Withdraw $500.00 from Robinhood to Savings …1234 (Rainy day)
  Withdrawable cash:  $1,250.00

  Note: A bank transfer takes a few business days to arrive.

To make this transfer, show this to the user. If they say yes, run:
  pyhood withdraw 500 --confirm 98fafd
  • The code is tied to the direction, the amount and the bank. A code for $50 will not move $500, and a code for a withdrawal will not make a deposit.
  • pyhood banks lists your linked banks by nickname, type and last four digits. With one bank linked there is nothing to choose. With more, add --bank and part of a nickname, a type, or the last four digits.
  • A withdrawal of more than your withdrawable cash is pointed out. Money from a recent sale or deposit takes time to become withdrawable.
  • pyhood cancel-transfer TRANSFER_ID cancels a transfer that has not gone through, at once. The ID is printed when the transfer is made.

pyhood has not made a transfer against Robinhood through these commands. The first step has been run live; the step that sends has only been tested against a stand-in.

docs.title: Setup and checks
docs.text: Command What it does pyhood setup Reports what is configured. See Setup pyhood authorize Asks you to log in, and saves the key Robinhood hands back. pyhood setup login is an older name for it pyhood authorize --window For an AI agent: opens a terminal window for the user to log in, and waits. docs.title: Scripts and agents

Short enough to be read whole pyhood guide python The reference for writing a script: how to log in, the main methods, and the fields of what they return

docs.title: When a command fails
docs.text:
A wrong confirmation code exits with status 2, and nothing is sent. Any other failure prints one line to standard error and exits with status 1:

  • Robinhood did not accept the order: ... with Robinhood's reason

  • pyhood is not authorized: ... followed by Run: pyhood authorize

  • Robinhood request failed: ...
  • No quote for XYZ. when a symbol is not recognized

docs.text: pyhood is in early development and we welcome contributions.

docs.title: Auditing Against the Live API
docs.text:
The tests mock Robinhood's responses. A parser that reads a field Robinhood does not send still passes, as long as its mock has the same made-up field. That has happened more than once.

scripts/field_audit.py checks the parsers against real responses. It runs the read-only methods on a live account, records every field they ask for, and reports the ones that were never there:

python scripts/field_audit.py          # problems only
python scripts/field_audit.py --all    # every method audited

It makes GET requests only, and prints field names and counts, never values, so its output is safe to paste into an issue. Run it before a release, and when you add a parser, add the method to its audit() function.

When you write a test for a parser, build the mock from a real response rather than from the fields the parser reads.

docs.title: Crypto Trading (Official API)
docs.text: pyhood wraps Robinhood's official, documented Crypto Trading API. This is separate from the unofficial API used for stocks and options.

docs.title: Key Differences
docs.text: Stocks/Options Crypto API Unofficial (reverse-engineered) Official (documented) Auth OAuth + device approval ED25519 API keys Base URL api.robinhood.com trading.robinhood.com Rate limits Unknown 100 req/min, 300 burst Human needed First login + expired refresh Never

docs.title: 1. Generate and register a key pair
docs.text:
Robinhood does not issue you a key pair. You generate one, register the public half at robinhood.com/account/crypto → API Trading → Add key, and Robinhood issues an API key that identifies it.

pyhood setup crypto

This generates the pair, shows you the public key to register, reads the API key back without echoing it, writes both to ~/.pyhood/crypto.env at mode 0600, and confirms with one signed read-only call that Robinhood accepts them. The private key is written straight to disk and never displayed.

See Setup for the full walkthrough, including rotation with --force.

docs.title: 2. Create a client
docs.text:
from pyhood.crypto import CryptoClient

crypto = CryptoClient()

Credentials resolve from RH_CRYPTO_API_KEY / RH_CRYPTO_PRIVATE_KEY, then from ~/.pyhood/crypto.env (override the path with PYHOOD_CRYPTO_ENV). Passing api_key= and private_key_base64= explicitly still works and takes precedence, but hardcoding them in source is how keys end up committed.

The private key is the credential

Anyone holding it can trade your crypto, and unlike a session token it cannot be refreshed — only revoked. Environment variables take precedence over the credentials file, so a stale export will silently shadow it; run pyhood setup to see which source is actually in use.

docs.title: Best Bid/Ask
docs.text:
quotes = crypto.get_best_bid_ask("BTC-USD", "ETH-USD")

for quote in quotes:
    print(f"{quote.symbol}: bid=${quote.bid:.2f} ask=${quote.ask:.2f}")

docs.title: Estimated Price
docs.text:
Get the expected execution price including fees:

docs.title: Authentication Details
docs.text:
Every request is signed with ED25519:

message = f"{api_key}{timestamp}{path}{method}{body}"
signature = ed25519_sign(message, private_key)

Three headers are sent:

Header Value x-api-key Your API key x-signature Base64-encoded ED25519 signature x-timestamp Unix timestamp (valid for 30 seconds)

pyhood handles all of this automatically.

docs.title: Rate Limits
docs.text:
The official API has documented rate limits:

  • 100 requests per minute per account
  • 300 requests per minute burst capacity
  • Token bucket with automatic refill

pyhood includes a built-in token bucket rate limiter that tracks your usage and prevents you from hitting limits.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: pyhood uses a clear exception hierarchy so you can catch errors at the right level of specificity.

docs.title: Exception Hierarchy
docs.text:
PyhoodError
├── AuthError
│   ├── LoginTimeoutError      — Login hung (device approval timeout)
│   ├── TokenExpiredError       — Refresh token expired, full re-login needed
│   ├── DeviceApprovalRequiredError — Approval sent but not completed
│   └── MFARequiredError        — SMS/email code needed
├── RateLimitError              — Too many requests (429)
├── APIError                    — Robinhood API returned an error
├── OrderError                  — Order placement/modification failed
└── SymbolNotFoundError         — Ticker not recognized

docs.title: Catch Everything
docs.text:
from pyhood.exceptions import PyhoodError

try:
    quote = client.get_quote("AAPL")
except PyhoodError as e:
    print(f"Something went wrong: {e}")

docs.title: Catch Specific Auth Errors
docs.text:
from pyhood.exceptions import LoginTimeoutError, MFARequiredError, TokenExpiredError

try:
    session = pyhood.login(username="...", password="...", timeout=90)
except LoginTimeoutError:
    print("Timed out — approve on your phone and try again")
except MFARequiredError:
    code = input("Enter MFA code: ")
    session = pyhood.login(username="...", password="...", mfa_code=code)
except TokenExpiredError:
    print("Refresh token expired — full re-login needed")

docs.title: Handle Rate Limits
docs.text:
from pyhood.exceptions import RateLimitError

try:
    quote = client.get_quote("AAPL")
except RateLimitError as e:
    print(f"Rate limited. Retry after: {e.retry_after}s")

docs.title: API Errors
docs.text:
from pyhood.exceptions import APIError

try:
    data = client.get_fundamentals("INVALID")
except APIError as e:
    print(f"API error {e.status_code}: {e}")
    print(f"Response: {e.response}")

docs.title: Convenience Aliases
docs.text:
For those who prefer shorter names:

from pyhood.exceptions import (
    LoginTimeout,          # → LoginTimeoutError
    TokenExpired,          # → TokenExpiredError
    DeviceApprovalRequired,# → DeviceApprovalRequiredError
    MFARequired,           # → MFARequiredError
    SymbolNotFound,        # → SymbolNotFoundError
)

docs.title: Automation Pattern
docs.text:
For unattended scripts (cron jobs, scanners), use this pattern:

import pyhood
from pyhood.exceptions import TokenExpiredError, AuthError

def get_session():
    """Get an authenticated session, refreshing if needed."""
    try:
        return pyhood.refresh()
    except TokenExpiredError:
        # Refresh token expired — need human intervention
        # Alert via email/SMS/Telegram
        raise
    except AuthError:
        # No stored session — need initial login
        raise

session = get_session()
client = pyhood.PyhoodClient(session)

docs.title: Fundamental Data Integration
docs.text: Pyhood provides fundamental data integration via the FundamentalData class, allowing you to screen stocks by financial ratios.

docs.title: FundamentalData Class
docs.text:
from pyhood.fundamentals import FundamentalData

fd = FundamentalData('AAPL')

# Access individual ratios
print(fd.pe_ratio)         # Trailing P/E ratio
print(fd.revenue_growth)   # Revenue growth (decimal, e.g. 0.15 = 15%)
print(fd.market_cap)       # Market capitalization in dollars
print(fd.sector)           # e.g. 'Technology'

# Get all available data as a dict
summary = fd.summary()
# {'ticker': 'AAPL', 'pe_ratio': 28.5, 'market_cap': 2800000000000, ...}

Data is fetched lazily from yfinance on first access and cached for the lifetime of the object.

docs.title: Available Properties
docs.text:
Property yfinance Key Description pe_ratio trailingPE Trailing price-to-earnings ratio forward_pe forwardPE Forward P/E based on analyst estimates pb_ratio priceToBook Price-to-book ratio debt_to_equity debtToEquity Total debt / total equity revenue_growth revenueGrowth YoY revenue growth (decimal) profit_margin profitMargins Net profit margin (decimal) market_cap marketCap Market capitalisation in USD beta beta Beta coefficient vs market dividend_yield dividendYield Annual dividend yield (decimal) sector sector GICS sector name industry industry Industry classification insider_buy_pct heldPercentInsiders % held by insiders institutional_pct heldPercentInstitutions % held by institutions short_ratio shortRatio Days to cover short interest earnings_growth earningsGrowth YoY earnings growth (decimal) current_ratio currentRatio Current assets / current liabilities free_cash_flow freeCashflow Free cash flow in USD

All properties return None if the data is not available from yfinance.

docs.title: Fundamental Filtering
docs.text:
Check whether a stock passes a set of criteria:

fd = FundamentalData('AAPL')
passes = fd.passes_filter({
    'pe_ratio': {'max': 30},
    'revenue_growth': {'min': 0.05},
    'market_cap': {'min': 100_000_000_000},
    'beta': {'min': 0.5, 'max': 2.0},
})

Each key is a property name. The value is a dict with 'min' and/or 'max'. If data for a property is missing (None), that filter is skipped (not failed).

docs.title: Futures Trading
docs.text: Pyhood provides access to Robinhood's futures trading API, including contract details, real-time quotes, order history, and P&L calculation.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
from pyhood import login, PyhoodClient

login("user@example.com", "password")
client = PyhoodClient()

# Get a futures contract
contract = client.get_futures_contract("ESH26")
print(f"{contract.name} — multiplier: {contract.multiplier}")

# Get a real-time quote
quote = client.get_futures_quote("ESH26")
print(f"Last: {quote.last_price}  Bid: {quote.bid}  Ask: {quote.ask}")

# Get filled orders and calculate P&L
orders = client.get_filled_futures_orders()
total_pnl = client.calculate_futures_pnl(orders=orders)
print(f"Realized P&L: ${total_pnl:.2f}")

docs.title: get_futures_account_id()
docs.text:
Auto-discovers the futures account ID by filtering Ceres accounts for accountType == 'FUTURES'.

Returns: str — the futures account ID.

Raises: APIError if no futures account exists.

docs.title: get_futures_contract(symbol)
docs.text:
Get contract details for a single futures symbol. Makes two requests: one for the contract and one for the product it belongs to (/ES for /ESH26), which is where the tick size, underlying and asset class are kept.

Parameters:

  • symbol (str): Futures symbol, e.g. 'ESH26' (E-mini S&P 500 March 2026).

Returns: FuturesContract with fields:

Field Type Description symbol str Contract symbol name str Human-readable name contract_id str Robinhood internal ID expiration str Expiration date (YYYY-MM-DD) tick_size float | None Minimum price increment multiplier float Contract multiplier status str Contract state (e.g. 'active') underlying str Product symbol (e.g. 'ES') asset_class str Product group (e.g. 'stock_index', 'energy', 'metals')

If the product lookup fails, the contract is still returned, with tick_size set to None and underlying and asset_class empty.

docs.title: get_futures_contracts(symbols)
docs.text:
Batch version — fetches contracts for multiple symbols. Skips failures silently.

Parameters:

  • symbols (list[str]): List of futures symbols.

Returns: dict[str, FuturesContract] mapping symbol to contract.

docs.title: get_futures_quote(symbol, include_fundamentals=False)
docs.text:
Get a real-time quote for a futures symbol. Resolves the symbol to a contract ID internally.

Parameters:

  • symbol (str): Futures symbol.
  • include_fundamentals (bool): Also fetch the session's high, low, previous close and volume. Robinhood's futures quote does not include them, so they are None without this. Costs one more request.

Returns: FuturesQuote with fields:

Field Type Description symbol str Contract symbol last_price float Last trade price bid float Current bid ask float Current ask high float | None Session high, with include_fundamentals=True low float | None Session low, with include_fundamentals=True prev_close float | None Previous close, with include_fundamentals=True volume int | None Trading volume, with include_fundamentals=True contract_id str Robinhood contract ID

Robinhood does not publish open interest for futures.

docs.title: get_futures_quotes(symbols, include_fundamentals=False)
docs.text:
Batch version — fetches quotes for multiple symbols. Skips failures silently.

Returns: dict[str, FuturesQuote]

docs.title: get_futures_orders(account_id=None)
docs.text:
Get all historical futures orders with automatic cursor-based pagination.

Parameters:

  • account_id (str, optional): Futures account ID. Auto-discovered if not provided.

Returns: list[FuturesOrder]

docs.title: get_filled_futures_orders(account_id=None)
docs.text: Same as get_futures_orders() but filtered to only filled orders.

docs.title: calculate_futures_pnl(orders=None, account_id=None)
docs.text:
Calculate total realized P&L across futures orders. Only counts CLOSING orders to avoid double-counting.

Parameters:

  • orders (list[FuturesOrder], optional): Pre-fetched orders. If None, fetches filled orders.
  • account_id (str, optional): Used to fetch orders if orders is None.

Returns: float — total realized P&L.

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text: Endpoint Description /arsenal/v1/futures/contracts/symbol/{symbol}/ Contract details /marketdata/futures/quotes/v1/ Real-time quotes (by contract ID) /ceres/v1/accounts/ Futures account discovery /ceres/v1/accounts/{id}/orders/ Order history (cursor-paginated)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Futures endpoints require the Rh-Contract-Protected: true header (set automatically).
  • The futures account is separate from the standard brokerage account — it has its own account ID discovered via the Ceres API.
  • Order pagination uses cursor-based pagination (same next URL pattern as standard Robinhood pagination).
  • P&L is nested inside orders at order.legs[0].executions[0].settlement.realized_pnl. The _extract_futures_pnl() method handles this.
  • Futures symbols follow the format: root + month code + year digits (e.g. ESH26 = E-mini S&P 500, March 2026).

docs.title: Have your AI agent do it
docs.text:
pyhood is built to be driven by an AI agent, so the quickest install is to hand it the job. Paste this into your agent:

Install pyhood for me. Follow the install steps in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamestford/pyhood/main/AGENTS.md

That file is written for AI agents. It tells yours to run the install script described under One command, and gives it rules that keep it from improvising: stop if a step fails, do not use pip or sudo, and do not install anything else.

An agent cannot log in for you. The login needs your password, which the agent must never see, and an approval on your phone. So the agent runs pyhood authorize --window, which opens a terminal window on your screen, titled "pyhood Authorization", and waits for you. You type in that window, and nothing you type passes through the agent. See First Login.

It needs uv (brew install uv on macOS). If uv is missing, the agent stops and asks you.

docs.title: One command
docs.text:
To do it yourself, run this in your own terminal, on macOS or Linux:

curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamestford/pyhood/main/install.sh | sh

The script does five things, in order:

  1. Looks for uv, the tool pyhood is installed with. If uv is missing, it asks before installing it.
  2. Creates ~/pyhood and installs pyhood into it, with the two commands under By hand. If pyhood is already there, it upgrades it.
  3. Links the command into ~/.local/bin, so that pyhood works from any folder.
  4. Runs pyhood authorize. See First Login.
  5. Runs pyhood verify, which reads live prices and changes nothing.

It never uses sudo. It installs pyhood, and uv only if you say yes.

Then open your AI agent in ~/pyhood and ask it something.

If Then uv is missing and you answer no Nothing is installed ~/pyhood exists and is not a pyhood install The script stops and changes nothing ~/.local/bin/pyhood is already something else It is left alone, and the script tells you to use ~/pyhood/bin/pyhood ~/.local/bin is not on your PATH The script says so. Add it to your PATH to type just pyhood The authorization does not finish pyhood stays installed. Do it later with pyhood authorize No terminal is attached, as when an agent runs it It installs pyhood and leaves the authorizing alone. The agent then opens the window with pyhood authorize --window

A download that is cut off partway runs nothing: the script does its work only on its last line.

docs.title: By hand
docs.text:
The same steps, typed yourself. pyhood installs into a folder of its own, and that folder is also where you work from:

uv venv --managed-python --python 3.14 ~/pyhood
uv pip install --python ~/pyhood/bin/python pyhood

That creates ~/pyhood:

In ~/pyhood What it is bin/pyhood The command bin/python A link to the Python pyhood runs on, which uv keeps in its own folder lib/ pyhood and what it depends on AGENTS.md Instructions an AI agent reads when it starts in this folder

Check it worked:

~/pyhood/bin/pyhood version

Why --managed-python

It tells uv to use a Python that it downloads and keeps for itself. Without it uv may borrow your system's or Homebrew's Python, and the install then breaks when that Python is upgraded or removed. Homebrew does remove old versions: an environment built on its Python 3.14 stopped working the day Homebrew moved to 3.15.

docs.title: Typing just pyhood
docs.text:
The install script does this for you. After the other installs, link the command into a folder that is on your PATH, and it works from anywhere:

ln -s ~/pyhood/bin/pyhood ~/.local/bin/pyhood

The rest of these docs write pyhood. If you skip the link, type ~/pyhood/bin/pyhood. Do not add ~/pyhood/bin itself to your PATH: that would also put its python ahead of your own.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
Run the install command again, or:

uv pip install --python ~/pyhood/bin/python --upgrade pyhood

docs.title: Running your scripts
docs.text:
A plain python cannot import pyhood, because pyhood lives in its own folder. Run scripts with:

pyhood run script.py

That uses the Python pyhood is installed in.

docs.title: Installing with pip instead
docs.text:
pyhood needs Python 3.10 or newer.

python3.14 -m venv ~/pyhood
~/pyhood/bin/python -m pip install --upgrade pip
~/pyhood/bin/python -m pip install pyhood

Substitute whichever interpreter you have; 3.10 through 3.14 are tested in CI. On Windows the commands are in pyhood\Scripts rather than pyhood/bin.

Name the Python version explicitly

A virtual environment inherits the version of the interpreter that creates it, and python3 on macOS is still 3.9. Using bare python3 there produces a 3.9 environment where the install fails with no matching distribution found, which reads like the package is missing rather than a version problem.

The environment depends on the Python that created it

If that Python is later removed, the environment stops working and has to be rebuilt.

Why not the system Python

Homebrew and Debian-based distributions mark their Python as externally managed, so installing into it is refused outright. Overriding that with --break-system-packages can break OS tooling that depends on the system packages.

To add pyhood to a project that already has its own environment, pip install pyhood there as usual.

For development:

git clone https://github.com/jamestford/pyhood.git
cd pyhood
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: First Login
docs.text: pyhood requires a one-time device approval through the Robinhood mobile app. After that, sessions refresh automatically.

docs.title: Step 1: Have Your Phone Ready
docs.text: Open the Robinhood app on your phone. You'll need to tap "Yes, it's me" when prompted.

docs.title: Step 2: Authorize
docs.text:
pyhood authorize

It asks for your username and password. The password is sent to Robinhood and is not saved. Robinhood then sends a prompt to its app on your phone: tap "Yes, it's me". What is saved is the key Robinhood hands back, in ~/.pyhood/session.json, readable only by you.

To remove the authorization later, open the Robinhood app and go to Account, then Menu, then Security and privacy, then Devices, and remove the device.

An AI agent runs pyhood authorize --window instead, which opens a terminal window on your screen with the same login in it. See Setup.

To log in from code instead:

import pyhood

session = pyhood.login(
    username="you@email.com",
    password="your_password",
    timeout=90,  # seconds to wait for device approval
)

Prefer the command where you can. A password written into a script tends to end up committed.

docs.title: Step 3: Use the Client
docs.text:
import pyhood
from pyhood.client import PyhoodClient

# No credentials needed — reuses the stored session.
client = PyhoodClient(pyhood.login())

# Get a stock quote
quote = client.get_quote("AAPL")
print(f"AAPL: ${quote.price:.2f}")

# Check your buying power
power = client.get_buying_power()
print(f"Buying power: ${power:,.2f}")

docs.title: Step 4: There Is No Step 4
docs.text:
Your session is cached at ~/.pyhood/session.json. Next time you call pyhood.login() or pyhood.refresh(), it reuses or refreshes the cached token automatically. No device approval needed.

# Subsequent runs — instant, no approval
session = pyhood.refresh()
client = PyhoodClient(session)

docs.title: Using pyhood With an AI Agent
docs.text:
pyhood is built to be driven by an AI agent. Open your agent in the install folder:

cd ~/pyhood

The install put an AGENTS.md there, which agents that follow that convention read when they start. It tells the agent to run pyhood guide. The guide prints the read-only commands (pyhood positions, pyhood orders and so on), the order commands and their rules, how to run a script, and the fields of what the methods return, all for the installed version. See Command Line.

To use pyhood from some other folder, put one line in that folder's AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md):

pyhood is installed on this machine. Run `pyhood guide` before using it.

An agent with your session can place real orders. Unless you have turned confirmation off, the guide tells it to show you an order and wait for a yes, but that is an instruction, not a lock.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
For scripts and automation, store credentials in a .env file:

# .env
RH_USERNAME=you@email.com
RH_PASSWORD=your_password

import os
import pyhood
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()
session = pyhood.login(
    username=os.getenv("RH_USERNAME"),
    password=os.getenv("RH_PASSWORD"),
)

Never commit .env files

pyhood's .gitignore blocks .env and *.json by default. Double-check before pushing to a remote repo.

docs.title: Robinhood IRA API — Reverse Engineering Notes
docs.text: Date: 2026-03-23 Account: Roth IRA (ira_roth) Account Number: Status: ✅ Fully working — stock and option orders confirmed

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The standard /accounts/ endpoint only returns the individual margin account (). The IRA account is invisible to /accounts/ — no query parameter (type, brokerage_account_type, all, include_retirement, page_size, etc.) makes it appear.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
The IRA account is discoverable via the Bonfire API:

GET https://bonfire.robinhood.com/accounts/unified/

This returns a results array with all accounts (individual + IRA). Each entry includes: - account_number / rhs_account_number - brokerage_account_type (e.g., "individual", "ira_roth") - account_buying_power, uninvested_cash, options_buying_power - equities.rhs_account_number — the account number for order routing - Full portfolio equity, market value, etc.

docs.title: Direct Access
docs.text:
Once you know the account number, you can access it directly through the standard API:

GET https://api.robinhood.com/accounts/<IRA_ACCOUNT_NUMBER>/

This returns the full account object (same schema as individual accounts), including: - type: "cash" (IRA accounts are always cash, no margin) - brokerage_account_type: "ira_roth" - buying_power: "7210.0000" - option_level: "option_level_2" (after enabling; null by default) - cash_balances (not margin_balances — IRA uses cash balances)

docs.title: 2. IRA Account Properties
docs.text: Field Value Notes account_number <IRA_ACCOUNT_NUMBER> type cash No margin on IRA brokerage_account_type ira_roth option_level option_level_2 (max) Level 3 capped to 2 buying_power 7210.0000 is_default false Individual is default is_original false sweep_enabled false margin_balances null Cash account only cash_balances {...} Has cash balance block

docs.title: Key Differences from Individual Account
docs.text:
• type is "cash" not "margin"
  • margin_balances is null; uses cash_balances instead
  • option_level maxes at option_level_2 (long puts/calls, covered calls/puts — no spreads, no naked)
  • option_trading_on_expiration_enabled defaults to false
  • is_default is false (individual account is default)

docs.title: 3. Enabling Options on IRA
docs.text: By default, option_level is null (options not enabled).

docs.title: Enable via PATCH
docs.text:
PATCH https://api.robinhood.com/accounts/<IRA_ACCOUNT_NUMBER>/
Content-Type: application/json

{"option_level": "option_level_3"}

The server caps it to option_level_2 for IRA accounts. This is the maximum allowed.

option_level_2 allows: - Buy calls (long calls) - Buy puts (long puts) - Sell covered calls - Sell cash-secured puts

option_level_2 does NOT allow: - Vertical spreads - Iron condors - Naked options

docs.title: 4. Placing Stock Orders on IRA
docs.text:
Standard /orders/ endpoint works. Just use the IRA account URL:

payload = {
    'account': 'https://api.robinhood.com/accounts/<IRA_ACCOUNT_NUMBER>/',
    'instrument': instrument_url,
    'symbol': 'AAPL',
    'type': 'limit',
    'time_in_force': 'gfd',
    'trigger': 'immediate',
    'price': '150.00',
    'quantity': '1.00000000',
    'side': 'buy',
    'ref_id': str(uuid.uuid4()),
}

r = session.post('https://api.robinhood.com/orders/', json=payload,
                  headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})

Important: Must send Content-Type: application/json header explicitly when posting JSON. The default pyhood session header is application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

docs.title: 5. Placing Option Orders on IRA
docs.text:
Standard /options/orders/ endpoint works with the IRA account URL:

payload = {
    'account': 'https://api.robinhood.com/accounts/<IRA_ACCOUNT_NUMBER>/',
    'direction': 'debit',  # REQUIRED for options (not 'side')
    'legs': [{
        'position_effect': 'open',
        'side': 'buy',
        'ratio_quantity': 1,
        'option': option_instrument_url,
    }],
    'price': '1.50',
    'quantity': '1',
    'time_in_force': 'gtc',
    'trigger': 'immediate',
    'type': 'limit',
    'override_day_trade_checks': False,
    'override_dtbp_checks': False,
    'ref_id': str(uuid.uuid4()),
}

r = session.post('https://api.robinhood.com/options/orders/', json=payload,
                  headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})

docs.title: Confirmed Working (201 response)
docs.text:
• Buy to open puts (long_put strategy) ✅
  • Order was accepted with state: "unconfirmed" then processed normally
  • Cancel via POST /options/orders/{id}/cancel/ works (200)

docs.title: Key Differences for Option Orders
docs.text:
• Use direction instead of side (unlike stock orders)
  • "debit" for buy orders
  • "credit" for sell orders (covered calls, CSPs)
  • The account field is the full URL: https://api.robinhood.com/accounts/<IRA_ACCOUNT_NUMBER>/

docs.title: Positions
docs.text: GET https://api.robinhood.com/positions/?account_number=<IRA_ACCOUNT_NUMBER>

docs.title: Option Positions
docs.text: GET https://api.robinhood.com/options/aggregate_positions/?account_numbers=<IRA_ACCOUNT_NUMBER>

docs.title: Option Orders
docs.text: GET https://api.robinhood.com/options/orders/?account_numbers=<IRA_ACCOUNT_NUMBER>

docs.title: Portfolio
docs.text:
GET https://api.robinhood.com/portfolios/<IRA_ACCOUNT_NUMBER>/

All standard endpoints work with the IRA account number as a filter parameter.

docs.text:
1. _get_account_url() in client.py — Currently calls /accounts/ which doesn't return IRA accounts. Two options:
  2. Use bonfire.robinhood.com/accounts/unified/ to discover all accounts

  3. Accept explicit account number and construct URL directly: f"https://api.robinhood.com/accounts/{account_number}/"

  4. order_option() — Uses side field where RH actually expects direction for options. The current code has "side": credit_or_debit which happens to work because the API accepts both for the individual account, but should be "direction" for correctness.

# In client.py

def get_all_accounts(self) -> list[dict]:
    """Get all accounts including IRA via bonfire endpoint."""
    r = self._session.get('https://bonfire.robinhood.com/accounts/unified/')
    return r.get('results', [])

def _get_account_url(self, account_number: str | None = None) -> str:
    if account_number:

    data = self._session.get_paginated(urls.ACCOUNTS)

• Option Level 2 max — IRA accounts cannot get level 3. No spreads, no naked options.
  • Cash account only — No margin, no instant deposits (1K max early access vs 48K on individual)

docs.title: Migrating from pyrh
docs.text:
A method-by-method map from pyrh to pyhood.

pyrh's last commit was August 2024. Its open issues include requests for options support (open since 2020) and fractional shares, both of which pyhood implements.

Three differences shape everything below.

One quote object instead of thirty accessors. pyrh exposes a method per field: ask_price(), bid_price(), last_trade_price(), previous_close(), each making its own request. pyhood fetches a Quote once and you read attributes off it.

Three order methods instead of thirteen. pyrh has place_market_buy_order, place_limit_buy_order, place_stop_loss_buy_order, place_stop_limit_buy_order and the four selling equivalents. pyhood has buy_stock(), sell_stock() and order_stock(); the order type follows from which arguments you pass.

Sessions renew without you. pyrh re-authenticates with stored credentials. pyhood persists the refresh token, so pyhood.refresh() needs no password and triggers no device approval prompt.

# pyrh
from pyrh import Robinhood
rh = Robinhood()
rh.login(username="you@email.com", password="...")
price = float(rh.last_trade_price("AAPL")[0][0])

# pyhood
import pyhood
from pyhood.client import PyhoodClient
client = PyhoodClient(pyhood.login())
price = client.get_quote("AAPL").price

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
pyrh pyhood Robinhood() then rh.login(username, password) pyhood.login(username, password) rh.logout() pyhood.logout() re-login with stored credentials pyhood.refresh(), no credentials, no device approval rh.get_url(url) client._session.get(url) for anything unwrapped

pyhood.login() with no arguments reuses the cached session and falls back to refresh() before ever asking for credentials. There is also a guided command:

pyhood authorize

docs.text:
pyrh's per-field accessors all collapse into one Quote:

quote = client.get_quote("AAPL")
pyrh pyhood quote_data(symbol) / get_quote(symbol) client.get_quote(symbol) quotes_data(symbols) / get_quote_list(...) client.get_quotes(symbols), returns dict[str, Quote] last_trade_price(symbol) quote.price ask_price(symbol) quote.ask bid_price(symbol) quote.bid previous_close(symbol) quote.prev_close symbol(symbol) quote.symbol last_updated_at(symbol) / last_updated_at_datetime(symbol) quote.timestamp, already a datetime get_historical_quotes(...) client.get_stock_historicals(symbol, interval, span, bounds) get_stock_marketdata(...) client.get_quotes(symbols) print_quote(symbol) / print_quotes(symbols) no equivalent, print the fields you want

Quote also carries change_pct. It has volume, pe_ratio, market_cap, high_52w and low_52w too, but Robinhood's quote does not include those, so they are None unless you pass include_fundamentals=True to get_quote() or get_quotes().

Not carried over: ask_size, bid_size, adjusted_previous_close and previous_close_date have no field on Quote. Reach for the raw endpoint through the session if you need them.

client.sell_stock("AAPL", 1, stop_price=140.00)  # stop

Also available and absent from pyrh: buy_stock_by_price() and sell_stock_by_price() for dollar-amount fractional orders (pyrh #200), trailing stops via trail_amount= or trail_percent=, extended and 24-hour sessions via market_hours=, and cancel_all_stock_orders().

docs.title: What pyhood adds
docs.text:
None of these exist in pyrh:

  • Futures contracts, quotes, orders, positions and P&L
  • The official Crypto Trading API, key-pair authenticated, separate from the unofficial endpoints
  • IRA and retirement accounts, discoverable and tradable via account_number=
  • Banking, ACH transfers, documents and statements
  • IPO Access
  • A stock screener (pyhood.screener.StockScreener), which is pyrh #309
  • Interest, fees and transfers
  • is_market_open(), aware of extended and 24-hour sessions

docs.title: Things to know
docs.text:
Sessions are stored as JSON, owner-only at ~/.pyhood/session.json, created 0600 inside a 0700 directory.

get_portfolio_historicals() raises APIError. Robinhood retired /portfolios/historicals/ and it now returns 404 for every parameter combination. get_portfolio_performance() calls the endpoint that replaced it, returning the chart view model unmapped, because its y values are returns rather than equity.

get_tags(), get_popularity() and the notification settings methods raise APIError too. Robinhood retired /midlands/tags/tag/, /instruments/<id>/popularity/ and /settings/notifications/, and all three return 404. The methods stay so that a call fails with an explanation. There is no replacement for popularity or notification settings. For tags, the Robinhood lists you follow in the app, such as its most popular list, come back from get_watchlists().

Fractional orders are unverified end to end. The payload and the rounding are covered by tests, but a fractional order is a market order and executes immediately, so the fill has never been exercised.

Questions about anything not covered here are welcome in Discussions.

docs.title: Migrating from robin_stocks
docs.text:
A function-by-function map from robin_stocks to pyhood.

Two differences shape everything below:

pyhood is object-oriented. robin_stocks is a module of free functions holding a global session. pyhood gives you a PyhoodClient you call methods on. This is the one change you cannot avoid.

pyhood returns typed objects. robin_stocks returns dicts (and often lists of dicts). pyhood returns dataclasses with annotated fields, so quote["last_trade_price"] becomes quote.price, and your editor can tell you what exists.

# robin_stocks
import robin_stocks.robinhood as r
r.login(username, password)
price = float(r.get_latest_price("AAPL")[0])

# pyhood
import pyhood
from pyhood.client import PyhoodClient
pyhood.login(username, password)
client = PyhoodClient()
price = client.get_quote("AAPL").price

After the first login, pyhood reuses the cached session and refreshes it silently — pyhood.refresh() needs no credentials and no device approval. That is the main reason people move.

docs.title: Orders — stocks
docs.text:
pyhood collapses robin_stocks' many order_buy_* / order_sell_* variants into three methods. Order type follows from which arguments you pass: omit price for a market order, pass price for a limit order, pass stop_price for a stop.

robin_stocks pyhood order_buy_market(symbol, qty) client.buy_stock(symbol, qty) order_sell_market(symbol, qty) client.sell_stock(symbol, qty) order_buy_limit(symbol, qty, price) client.buy_stock(symbol, qty, price=price) order_sell_limit(symbol, qty, price) client.sell_stock(symbol, qty, price=price) order_buy_stop_loss(symbol, qty, stop) client.buy_stock(symbol, qty, stop_price=stop) order_sell_stop_loss(symbol, qty, stop) client.sell_stock(symbol, qty, stop_price=stop) order_buy_stop_limit(symbol, qty, price, stop) client.buy_stock(symbol, qty, price=price, stop_price=stop) order_sell_stop_limit(symbol, qty, price, stop) client.sell_stock(symbol, qty, price=price, stop_price=stop) order(...) client.order_stock(symbol, qty, side, ...) get_all_stock_orders() client.get_stock_orders() get_stock_order_info(order_id) client.get_order(order_id) cancel_stock_order(order_id) client.cancel_order(order_id) cancel_all_stock_orders() client.cancel_all_stock_orders()

Trailing stops and fractional orders:

robin_stocks pyhood order_buy_trailing_stop(symbol, qty, trailAmount) client.buy_stock(symbol, qty, trail_amount=amt) — see note order_sell_trailing_stop(symbol, qty, trailAmount) client.sell_stock(symbol, qty, trail_amount=amt) — see note order_trailing_stop(..., trailType='percentage') client.buy_stock(..., trail_percent=pct) — see note order_buy_fractional_by_price(symbol, dollars) client.buy_stock_by_price(symbol, dollars) order_sell_fractional_by_price(symbol, dollars) client.sell_stock_by_price(symbol, dollars) order_buy_fractional_by_quantity(symbol, qty) client.buy_stock(symbol, qty) — fractional quantities are accepted

A note on order_form_version. Robinhood versions its order form and refuses orders from clients sending an old value or none, with:

Your app version is missing important stock trading updates.
You can still place orders on the web.

This reads like a client-version block but is not — it means the order form version. pyhood sends 7, captured from the web client. Tested against the live API, any value from 2 upward is accepted; 1 and omitting the field are refused.

robin_stocks sends 4 on ordinary stock orders, so those are unaffected. It omits the field on order_trailing_stop, so trailing stops fail there with this error. Option orders do not require the field at all.

If that message reappears, Robinhood has moved to a newer form version: raise ORDER_FORM_VERSION in pyhood/client.py. pyhood's error message says so explicitly rather than failing opaquely.

Order history takes start_date= to avoid paging through years of orders:

client.get_stock_orders(start_date="2026-01-01")

docs.title: Extended and 24-hour sessions
docs.text:
pyhood accepts a market_hours argument on stock orders, which robin_stocks exposes the same way:

robin_stocks pyhood order(..., market_hours='extended_hours') client.buy_stock(..., market_hours="extended_hours") order(..., market_hours='all_day_hours') client.buy_stock(..., market_hours="all_day_hours")

Valid values are regular_hours, extended_hours and all_day_hours. Robinhood rejects an order whose session disagrees with its extended_hours flag, so pyhood derives the flag from the session rather than letting the two drift apart.

Omitting the argument sends no field and preserves the previous behaviour.

docs.title: Options chains and contracts
docs.text:
robin_stocks pyhood get_chains(symbol) client.get_options_expirations(symbol), then get_options_chain(symbol, expiration) find_tradable_options(symbol, expiration, type) client.get_options_chain(symbol, expiration, option_type=type) find_options_by_expiration(symbol, exp) client.get_options_chain(symbol, exp) find_options_by_strike(symbol, strike) filter the chain — see below find_options_by_expiration_and_strike(symbol, exp, strike) filter the chain — see below get_option_historicals(...) client.get_option_historicals(...)

expiration is required. pyhood fetches one expiration at a time rather than the whole chain, and there is no strike filter — filter the contracts yourself:

chain = client.get_options_chain("AAPL", "2026-09-18")
at_strike = [c for c in chain.calls if c.strike == 200.0]

The chain separates chain.calls and chain.puts rather than returning one mixed list; option_type="call" limits which of the two is populated.

To scan every expiration, loop over get_options_expirations(symbol). This is more calls than robin_stocks' find_options_by_strike, which searched across expirations for you.

Chain results carry Greeks, volume and open interest as typed fields. Index options (SPX, NDX, VIX, RUT, XSP) work through the same method.

chain = client.get_options_chain("AAPL", expiration="2026-04-17")

docs.title: Exploring Contracts
docs.text:
Each contract is an OptionContract dataclass with full Greeks:

for call in chain.calls:
    if call.delta is None:
        continue  # no greeks published, see below
    print(
        f"  {call.strike:>8.2f} call | "
        f"Mark: ${call.mark:.2f} | "
        f"IV: {call.iv:.0%} | "
        f"Delta: {call.delta:+.2f} | "
        f"Vol: {call.volume:,} | "
        f"OI: {call.open_interest:,}"
    )

The greeks are None when Robinhood publishes none, which it does for every contract on its expiration day: prices keep updating, greeks go null. None is kept distinct from 0.0, because zero is a real delta for a far out-of-the-money contract. Check for None before doing arithmetic or formatting.

docs.title: Index Options (SPX, NDX, VIX, RUT)
docs.text:
pyhood supports index options out of the box. Use the base index symbol — pyhood handles the API differences automatically.

Index options use different Robinhood API paths than equity options: instrument lookup goes through /indexes/ instead of /instruments/, chains return tradable_chain_ids (plural) instead of tradable_chain_id, and the chain_symbol sent to /options/instruments/ is a variant of the ticker (e.g. SPXW for SPX weekly options, NDXP for NDX).

You don't need to worry about any of this — just pass the base symbol:

# Index options work exactly like equity options
chain = client.get_options_chain("SPX", expiration="2026-04-17")
for call in chain.calls:
    print(f"  {call.strike} call | IV: {call.iv} | Delta: {call.delta}")

# Expirations
expirations = client.get_options_expirations("SPX")

# Order placement
order = client.buy_option(
    symbol="SPX", strike=5800.0, expiration="2026-04-17",
    option_type="call", quantity=1, price=42.50,
)

Supported index symbols: SPX, NDX, VIX, RUT, XSP

docs.text:
pyhood supports options trading in IRA accounts. Pass account_number to buy_option or sell_option:

order = client.buy_option(
    symbol="NKE", strike=55.0, expiration="2026-04-02",
    option_type="call", quantity=3, price=1.60,
    account_number="YOUR_IRA_ACCOUNT",
)

IRA accounts are limited to Level 2 options: long calls, long puts, covered calls, and cash-secured puts. Spreads and multi-leg strategies are not available. See Account docs for details.

Use get_option_positions() to get fully resolved option positions with live market data, P&L, and Greeks:

positions = client.get_option_positions()

for p in positions:
    print(
        f"{p.symbol} ${p.strike} {p.option_type} exp {p.expiration} | "
        f"qty: {p.quantity} | "
        f"cost: ${p.cost_basis:.0f} | "
        f"value: ${p.current_value:.0f} | "
        f"P&L: ${p.unrealized_pl:.2f} ({p.unrealized_pl_pct:+.1f}%) | "
        f"delta: {p.delta} | IV: {p.iv}"
    )

positions = client.get_option_positions(account_number="YOUR_IRA_ACCOUNT")

Robinhood's quote does not include these. They come from the fundamentals endpoint, so volume, pe_ratio, market_cap, high_52w and low_52w are None on a plain quote. Pass include_fundamentals=True to fill them, at the cost of one more request:

quote = client.get_quote("AAPL", include_fundamentals=True)

print(f"PE Ratio:   {quote.pe_ratio}")
print(f"Market Cap: {quote.market_cap:,.0f}")
